title: 2003 AMC 10A 18
statement: What is the sum of the reciprocals of the roots of the equation \[\dfrac{2003}{2004}x + 1 + \dfrac{1}{x} = 0?\]

solutions.text:
Let \(a = \dfrac{2003}{2004}.\) Multiplying the equation by \(x\) gives \(ax^2 + x + 1 = 0.\)

If the roots are \(r\) and \(s,\) then by Vieta’s formulas \(r + s = -\dfrac{1}{a}\) and \(rs = \dfrac{1}{a}.\)

The sum of reciprocals is \(\dfrac{1}{r} + \dfrac{1}{s} = \dfrac{r + s}{rs} = \dfrac{-\frac{1}{a}}{\frac{1}{a}} = -1.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Multiply through by \(x\) to get a quadratic \(ax^2 + x + 1 = 0\) with \(a = \dfrac{2003}{2004}\)
If the roots are \(r\) and \(s,\) their reciprocal sum is \(\dfrac{r + s}{rs},\) and by Vieta \(r + s = -\dfrac{1}{a},\) \(rs = \dfrac{1}{a}\)
